source_bias_notes: Vendor-sponsored Total Economic Impact studies project theoretical multi-hundred percent ROI figures based on optimistic efficiency assumptions rather than verified balance-sheet reductions.

Management consultancy publications systematically emphasize that seventy percent of transformation effort lies in organizational redesign, aligning with their commercial operating model advisory practices.
Data security and DSPM vendors heavily emphasize tenant oversharing and shadow AI statistics to generate demand for automated classification software.
synthesis.change_since_last_run: Workflow agent impact is increasingly bifurcated between high-volume operational deflection, such as customer service and inventory replenishment, and highly constrained regulated domains. Desktop copilots continue to show solid uptake in basic meeting synthesis, but broader horizontal rollouts face heightened scrutiny over tenant permission exposure and rapid user disengagement. Auditability registries and non-human identity governance have emerged as critical structural gating items for autonomous deployment.
open_questions: At what threshold of process complexity does the cost of human-in-the-loop exception handling exceed the savings from autonomous agent deflection?

evidence.stated_factor: Proven production-scale productivity and inventory precision outcomes

evidence.inference: Cybersecurity concerns and implementation cost are cited as inhibitors, representing threat model/identity concerns and ROI/upfront spend uncertainty.
evidence.framing_bias: PwC explicitly dismisses cybersecurity and cost as 'safe excuses' to persuade hesitant buyers to initiate paid implementations.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of trust and governance in high-stakes autonomous decisions
evidence.evidence_quote: Trust lags for high-stakes use cases, underscoring the need for responsible AI.
evidence.statistic: 28% lack trust in agentic execution
evidence.title: PwC's AI Agent Survey: Key Trends About AI Agents in the Enterprise
evidence.methodology: survey of 300 US senior executives
evidence.inference: Trust deficits in high-stakes decisions (like underwriting and AML triage) stem from an inability to explain, audit, and reversibly control agent actions under strict regulatory standards.
evidence.framing_bias: Frames auditability and compliance gaps under the softer, brand-safe label of 'trust' and 'responsible AI'.

evidence.stated_factor: Reduced agent cognitive overload and tool fatigue during live interactions
evidence.evidence_quote: Companies currently deploying GenAI are 35% less likely to report agents are overwhelmed by information they're working with during calls.
evidence.statistic: 35% less likely to report agents are overwhelmed
evidence.title: 2024 Global Contact Center Survey: The Service Innovator Advantage
evidence.methodology: Survey of 600 senior contact center leaders in companies with 1,000+ employees and $100M+ revenue across US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan
evidence.inference: Alleviating agent cognitive overload and tool fatigue removes workplace friction and burnout, driving adoption through improved employee experience and redesigned workflows.
evidence.framing_bias: Focuses on frontline employee well-being as a driver to soften enterprise workforce reduction narratives.

evidence.stated_factor: Higher customer satisfaction (CSAT) and frontline employee retention
use_case_ids: Autonomous Customer Service Voice & Chat Agents
evidence.evidence_quote: These organizations achieved 57% more of their service strategies in 2023 versus other survey respondents and were much more likely to report excellent customer satisfaction (4.6x more likely) and excellent employee satisfaction (2.5x more likely).
evidence.statistic: 4.6x more likely to report excellent CSAT; 2.5x more likely to report excellent employee satisfaction
evidence.title: 2024 Global Contact Center Survey: The Service Innovator Advantage
evidence.methodology: Survey of 600 senior contact center leaders in companies with 1,000+ employees and $100M+ revenue across US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan
evidence.inference: Substantially higher customer satisfaction (4.6x) and employee retention (2.5x) represent tangible business value and organizational stability.
evidence.framing_bias: Correlational survey findings from 'innovators' are framed as direct causal benefits of GenAI deployment.

evidence.stated_factor: Lower cost per assisted contact through omnichannel workflow integration
use_case_ids: Omnichannel Customer Support Ticket Triage & Routing
evidence.evidence_quote: One in 3 companies has implemented omnichannel integration tools, resulting in a 9% lower cost per assisted contact.
evidence.statistic: 9% lower cost per assisted contact
evidence.title: 2024 Global Contact Center Survey: The Service Innovator Advantage
evidence.methodology: Survey of 600 senior contact center leaders in companies with 1,000+ employees and $100M+ revenue across US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan
evidence.inference: A 9% cost reduction per assisted contact demonstrates direct ROI achieved through unified omnichannel system integration.
evidence.framing_bias: Positions tech-led integration tools as the primary driver of contact center cost efficiency.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of cross-functional enterprise strategy for self-service automation
use_case_ids: Autonomous Customer Service Voice & Chat Agents
evidence.evidence_quote: Twenty-six percent of companies have a well-defined cross-functional strategy to improve self-service capabilities. Twenty percent are currently investing in better self-service capabilities (with an additional 30% planning to invest by the end of 2024).
evidence.statistic: Only 26% of companies have a well-defined cross-functional strategy
evidence.title: 2024 Global Contact Center Survey: The Service Innovator Advantage
evidence.methodology: Survey of 600 senior contact center leaders in companies with 1,000+ employees and $100M+ revenue across US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan
evidence.inference: The absence of a defined cross-functional self-service strategy indicates fragmented leadership ownership and lack of centralized operating model governance.
evidence.framing_bias: Frames strategy absence as an advisory opportunity for cross-functional operating model consulting.

evidence.stated_factor: Regulatory non-compliance awareness and outdated governance policies
evidence.evidence_quote: While 49% of organizations have policies in place to regulate AI use among employees, only a quarter believe those policies are future-proof. Meanwhile, 57% of HR professionals in states with workforce-related AI regulations are not aware of those rules. Among those who are aware, only 12% have taken steps to ensure compliance.
evidence.statistic: 57% of HR professionals unaware of state workforce AI rules; only 12% taking compliance steps
evidence.title: The State of AI in HR in 2026: 5 Critical Insights for CHROs
evidence.methodology: Survey of more than 1,900 HR professionals
evidence.inference: Unawareness of workplace AI laws and reliance on outdated policies highlight critical regulatory compliance and policy governance gaps.
evidence.framing_bias: Industry body emphasizes regulatory exposure to promote HR policy standardisation and training programs.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of formal ROI measurement and business value tracking
evidence.evidence_quote: Even more concerning, 56% of HR functions do not formally measure the success of their AI investments, and only 16% use ROI as a metric. This suggests many organizations are deploying AI tactically without fully understanding or capturing its business impact.
evidence.statistic: 56% do not formally measure success; only 16% track ROI
evidence.title: The State of AI in HR in 2026: 5 Critical Insights for CHROs
evidence.methodology: Survey of more than 1,900 HR professionals
evidence.inference: The lack of formal ROI metrics (only 16% tracking ROI) and business impact tracking reflects weak business case discipline and tactical operating models.
evidence.framing_bias: Positions tactical experimentation as deficient to advocate for formal business-case and governance frameworks.

evidence.stated_factor: Exclusion of HR functional leadership from enterprise AI strategy
evidence.evidence_quote: More than half of organizations (52%) do not involve HR in AI strategy or vision. Leadership of AI initiatives typically sits with IT, legal, or cross-functional teams.
evidence.statistic: 52% do not involve HR in AI strategy
evidence.title: The State of AI in HR in 2026: 5 Critical Insights for CHROs
evidence.methodology: Survey of more than 1,900 HR professionals
evidence.inference: Excluding HR leadership from AI strategy is a classic operating model failure where AI initiatives remain siloed in IT/legal without functional stakeholder ownership.
evidence.framing_bias: Advocates for HR functional relevance and seat at the executive AI strategy table.

evidence.stated_factor: Efficiency and work quality improvements across recruitment and HR processes
evidence.evidence_quote: AI is delivering tangible performance gains, with 87% of HR professionals reporting improved efficiency, 75% improved work quality, and 70% increased creativity... adoption is concentrated in a few areas: recruiting (27%), HR technology (21%), and learning and development (17%).
evidence.statistic: 87% report improved efficiency; 75% report improved work quality
evidence.title: The State of AI in HR in 2026: 5 Critical Insights for CHROs
evidence.methodology: Survey of more than 1,900 HR professionals
evidence.inference: Reported efficiency gains (87%) and work quality improvements (75%) provide demonstrable user-level productivity and performance proof points.
evidence.framing_bias: Relies on subjective self-reported efficiency and creativity metrics rather than audited economic return.

evidence.stated_factor: Inadequate IAM systems and governance for autonomous agent identities
evidence.evidence_quote: Only 18% of respondents say they are “highly confident” their current IAM systems can manage agent identities effectively. 35% express only moderate confidence and 29% express slight confidence. Another 18% report no or uncertain confidence.
evidence.statistic: Only 18% highly confident in IAM systems for agents
evidence.title: Securing Autonomous AI Agents
evidence.methodology: Survey report commissioned by Strata exploring enterprise autonomous AI agent security and IAM
evidence.inference: Low confidence in existing IAM systems to govern autonomous agent identities directly points to non-human identity, credential scoping, and privilege management vulnerabilities.
evidence.framing_bias: Security alliance highlights IAM deficiencies to stimulate demand for specialized machine identity and agent security software.

evidence.stated_factor: Limited agent discovery and lack of real-time inventory registries
evidence.evidence_quote: Only 21% of organizations maintain a real-time registry or inventory of their agents. 32% rely on non-real-time records, another 32% plan to build one within the next year, and 8% have no registry at all.
evidence.statistic: Only 21% maintain a real-time agent registry
evidence.title: Securing Autonomous AI Agents
evidence.methodology: Survey report commissioned by Strata exploring enterprise autonomous AI agent security and IAM
evidence.inference: Lack of real-time agent registries prevents organizations from maintaining an auditable inventory or tracking shadow agent activities and risks.
evidence.framing_bias: Frames uninventoried agents as an urgent enterprise risk to promote continuous discovery and cataloging tools.

evidence.stated_factor: Expanding production deployment and active piloting of autonomous AI agents
evidence.evidence_quote: 40% of organizations already have agents in production. Another 31% are running pilots or tests, with 19% planning deployment within the next year.
evidence.statistic: 40% in production; 31% running pilots or tests
evidence.title: Securing Autonomous AI Agents
evidence.methodology: Survey report commissioned by Strata exploring enterprise autonomous AI agent security and IAM
evidence.inference: Transitioning agents from pilots to production reflects maturing operational governance and validated business utility across enterprise workflows.
evidence.framing_bias: Highlights rapid production ramp (40%) to create market urgency and drive enterprise adoption of security frameworks.

evidence.stated_factor: Shift from manual sample-checking to 100% real-time transaction audit coverage
evidence.evidence_quote: Traditional manual audits review a statistical sample of transactions. AI audit agents analyze 100% of submissions in real time, scanning for fake receipts, duplicate submissions and policy violations, delivering complete coverage without adding headcount.
evidence.statistic: 100% submission analysis
evidence.title: How AI Agents Are Automating Expense Reports and Saving Travelers Time
evidence.methodology: Industry analysis synthesizing American Express Trendex survey (513 financial leaders), Forrester TEI study, and Ramp empirical dataset (50,000 businesses)
evidence.inference: Moving from manual sample checks to 100% automated audit coverage solves an auditability and risk assurance problem while eliminating marginal headcount costs.
evidence.framing_bias: Presents 100% automated auditing as purely beneficial without noting false-positive handling or employee friction.

evidence.stated_factor: Rising spend complexity driving finance adoption of automated fraud and policy auditing
evidence.evidence_quote: An American Express Trendex survey of 513 financial decision makers found that 52% already use AI to manage expenses, most commonly for detecting fraud, categorizing expenses and capturing receipt data. Another 40% say they plan to. The survey found 66% of businesses struggle to keep up with spending complexity
evidence.statistic: 52% currently use AI; 66% struggle with spending complexity
evidence.title: How AI Agents Are Automating Expense Reports and Saving Travelers Time
evidence.methodology: Industry analysis synthesizing American Express Trendex survey (513 financial leaders), Forrester TEI study, and Ramp empirical dataset (50,000 businesses)
evidence.inference: Complexity in financial spend forces adoption of automated fraud detection and policy enforcement to maintain risk auditability and control costs.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor survey frames spend complexity as an inevitable crisis solvable by automated expense intelligence.

evidence.stated_factor: Automated point-of-sale policy enforcement and auditable compliance verification
evidence.evidence_quote: Ramp’s research across 50,000 businesses found that companies using agents for expense management saw out-of-policy spend event rates fall 62% and policy flag rates drop 60% over two years. The Policy Agent screens every transaction with 99% accuracy and declines out-of-policy purchases at the point of sale. Every decision produces an audit trail that holds up to internal review and external compliance checks.
evidence.statistic: 62% drop in out-of-policy spend events; 99% screening accuracy
evidence.title: How AI Agents Are Automating Expense Reports and Saving Travelers Time
evidence.methodology: Industry analysis synthesizing American Express Trendex survey (513 financial leaders), Forrester TEI study, and Ramp empirical dataset (50,000 businesses)
evidence.inference: Point-of-sale policy enforcement with a 99% accuracy rate and audit trails addresses risk auditability, fraud prevention, and compliance verification.
evidence.framing_bias: Fintech platform highlights proprietary policy engine accuracy to showcase enterprise control capabilities.

evidence.stated_factor: Substantial reduction in audit cycle time and submission friction
evidence.evidence_quote: A 2025 Forrester TEI study cited by the article found that organizations using Navan saw employees save 24 minutes per expense submission and finance teams spend 40% less time on auditing and reconciliation.
evidence.statistic: 40% less time spent by finance teams on auditing and reconciliation; 24 minutes saved per submission
evidence.title: How AI Agents Are Automating Expense Reports and Saving Travelers Time
evidence.methodology: Industry analysis synthesizing American Express Trendex survey (513 financial leaders), Forrester TEI study, and Ramp empirical dataset (50,000 businesses)
evidence.inference: Saving 24 minutes per submission and reducing finance audit time by 40% represents concrete time-to-value ROI and eliminates employee friction.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor-sponsored Forrester TEI study highlights favorable time-savings metrics to demonstrate quantifiable ROI.

evidence.stated_factor: Elimination of manual case logging and administrative wrap-up tasks
evidence.evidence_quote: Currently, agents spend just 39% of their time servicing customers amid competing demands like internal meetings, administrative tasks, and manually logging case notes. Ninety-three percent of service professionals at organizations with AI say the technology saves them time.
evidence.statistic: Agents spend just 39% of time servicing customers; 93% say AI saves time
evidence.title: Salesforce State of Service, 6th Edition
evidence.methodology: Double-anonymous survey of over 5,500 service professionals across 30 countries
evidence.inference: Automating administrative wrap-up and CRM note logging recovers human capacity (from 39% service time), directly driving operating efficiency and ROI.
evidence.framing_bias: Salesforce emphasizes time spent in CRM administration to justify enterprise investment in its Agentforce/Service Cloud automation.

evidence.stated_factor: Commercial shift from cost centre to revenue generation and churn retention
use_case_ids: Proactive Retention & Churn Prevention Outreach Agent
evidence.evidence_quote: Eighty-five percent of service decision makers now say their teams are expected to contribute a larger slice of revenue over the coming year through upselling, cross-selling, and customer retention.
evidence.statistic: 85% expected to contribute a larger slice of revenue
evidence.title: Salesforce State of Service, 6th Edition
evidence.methodology: Double-anonymous survey of over 5,500 service professionals across 30 countries
evidence.inference: Transforming customer service from a cost center into a proactive revenue and retention driver is an operating model and revenue-focused strategy shift.
evidence.framing_bias: Salesforce frames customer service as a profit center to expand software budget allocation beyond traditional cost-cutting limits.

evidence.stated_factor: Data fragmentation across disparate enterprise systems requiring integration investment
use_case_ids: Autonomous Customer Service Voice & Chat Agents
Omnichannel Customer Support Ticket Triage & Routing
evidence.evidence_quote: For both AI and employees, personalizing service interactions requires customer knowledge, which often is drawn from many different data sources. Empowering AI and employees with a complete view is a clear priority for decision makers, 83% of whom plan to boost investments in data integration over the next year.
evidence.statistic: 83% plan to boost investments in data integration
evidence.title: Salesforce State of Service, 6th Edition
evidence.methodology: Double-anonymous survey of over 5,500 service professionals across 30 countries
evidence.inference: Customer service agents require unified context, but enterprise data is trapped in fragmented legacy and SaaS silos without established connectors.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor highlights data fragmentation to promote its own unified data and integration platform (Data Cloud).

evidence.stated_factor: Escalation of case complexity as routine interactions are deflected
evidence.evidence_quote: 65% of agents, and 66% of mobile workers, say their cases are more complex than a year ago.
evidence.statistic: 65% of agents and 66% of mobile workers report higher case complexity
evidence.title: Salesforce State of Service, 6th Edition
evidence.methodology: Double-anonymous survey of over 5,500 service professionals across 30 countries
evidence.inference: Deflecting tier-1 routine inquiries concentrates complex edge cases among human workers, exposing skills gaps and requiring operating model adjustments.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor frames case complexity as a reason to deploy real-time agent assist and copilot software.

evidence.stated_factor: Siloed single-use-case pilot approach without end-to-end process redesign
evidence.evidence_quote: Most organisations are still trying to justify AI investments one use case at a time. Our research shows the greatest returns come when organisations redesign procurement processes with AI as a key enabler, allowing better decisions to build value throughout the end-to-end process.
evidence.title: The Hackett Group: Integrating AI Into Procurement Practices
evidence.methodology: Benchmark research and empirical study of enterprise procurement organizations (AI World Class Procurement Benchmarks)
evidence.inference: Treating AI as point-solution pilots rather than executing holistic process redesign across the value chain prevents organizations from capturing value.

evidence.stated_factor: Executive expectation of structural transformation in procurement operations
evidence.evidence_quote: A separate 2025 study by The Hackett Group found that 64% of procurement executives expect generative AI to fundamentally transform their teams' operations within the next five years.
evidence.statistic: 64% of procurement executives
evidence.title: The Hackett Group: Integrating AI Into Procurement Practices
evidence.methodology: Benchmark research and empirical study of enterprise procurement organizations (AI World Class Procurement Benchmarks)
evidence.inference: C-suite and functional executive commitment to fundamental operational transformation acts as a primary catalyst for agentic adoption.

evidence.stated_factor: Shadow AI usage compromising customer data privacy, security, and compliance
evidence.evidence_quote: While 90% of CX Trendsetters report positive returns on AI tools for agents, as copilots improve both the customer journey and operational agility, the use of shadow AI–external tools unapproved for agent use–has jumped up to 250% year-on-year in some industries. This is putting customer privacy, security and service quality at risk.
evidence.statistic: Shadow AI usage jumped up to 250% year-on-year
evidence.title: Zendesk 2025 Customer Experience (CX) Trends Report
evidence.methodology: Survey of 5,100 consumers and 5,400 CX leaders, agents, and tech buyers across 22 countries
evidence.inference: Frontline staff adopting unsanctioned external tools creates credential exposure, data privacy leaks, and governance violations.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor highlights shadow AI risks to persuade IT and CX leaders to purchase governed enterprise CX AI platforms.

evidence.stated_factor: Agent sentiment favorability toward AI copilots offloading routine work
evidence.evidence_quote: Seventy-three percent of agents believe that having an AI copilot would help them do their job better, freeing them up to focus on more complex issues, enabling a smooth and scalable experience.
evidence.statistic: 73% of agents believe AI copilot helps them do their job better
evidence.title: Zendesk 2025 Customer Experience (CX) Trends Report
evidence.methodology: Survey of 5,100 consumers and 5,400 CX leaders, agents, and tech buyers across 22 countries
evidence.inference: Willingness and positive sentiment from frontline agents to offload repetitive tasks lowers cultural friction and accelerates copilot rollout.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor emphasizes frontline enthusiasm to counter enterprise concerns regarding user resistance or job replacement fears.

evidence.stated_factor: Customer churn risk from failed or frustrating automated AI interactions
use_case_ids: Autonomous Customer Service Voice & Chat Agents
evidence.evidence_quote: As their expectations for great service rises, consumers have increasingly low tolerance for bad experiences, with 63% willing to switch to a competitor due to just one bad experience - a trend that's grown by 9% year-on-year.
evidence.statistic: 63% willing to switch after just one bad experience
evidence.title: Zendesk 2025 Customer Experience (CX) Trends Report
evidence.methodology: Survey of 5,100 consumers and 5,400 CX leaders, agents, and tech buyers across 22 countries
evidence.inference: Unreliable or inaccurate agentic customer interactions risk direct brand defection, making model quality and failure guardrails critical.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor uses consumer intolerance for bad service to argue for enterprise-grade, high-reliability AI solutions.

evidence.stated_factor: Cycle time reduction and accuracy improvement in underwriting submissions
evidence.evidence_quote: For standard policies, average decision time dropped from 3-5 days to about 12 minutes while maintaining 99.3% accuracy [1]. Even in complex cases, AI reduced processing time by 31% and improved accuracy by 43%.
evidence.statistic: decision time dropped from 3-5 days to 12 minutes with 99.3% accuracy; complex case time reduced by 31%
evidence.title: Agentic AI for Commercial Insurance Underwriting with Adversarial Self-Critique
evidence.methodology: academic study and experimental evaluation using 500 expert-validated commercial underwriting cases
evidence.inference: Slashing underwriting submission review times from days to minutes with verified high accuracy proves productivity gains and cost ROI.

evidence.stated_factor: Ineffective legacy systems, poor data quality, and limited data accessibility
evidence.evidence_quote: Most underwriting leaders identify ineffective legacy systems, poor data quality, and limited data accessibility as impediments. AI adoption has been limited and fragmented, automating only segments of the process rather than entire workflows.
evidence.title: Agentic AI for Commercial Insurance Underwriting with Adversarial Self-Critique
evidence.methodology: academic study and experimental evaluation using 500 expert-validated commercial underwriting cases
evidence.inference: Inflexible core insurance legacy systems and fragmented, uncurated policyholder data prevent automated end-to-end underwriting execution.

evidence.stated_factor: Hallucination risks and regulatory human oversight mandates
evidence.evidence_quote: Regulatory bodies require human oversight for high-risk AI systems [3, 4]. AI failure modes pose real risks. Without mitigation, LLMs hallucinate frequently. Rates reach 15% in finance-related tasks.
evidence.statistic: Hallucination rates reach 15% in finance-related tasks
evidence.title: Agentic AI for Commercial Insurance Underwriting with Adversarial Self-Critique
evidence.methodology: academic study and experimental evaluation using 500 expert-validated commercial underwriting cases
evidence.inference: High hallucination rates in financial computations paired with mandatory human oversight regulations impede autonomous underwriting sign-off.

evidence.stated_factor: Decreased software delivery throughput and stability from larger batch sizes and review bottlenecks
evidence.evidence_quote: Contrary to expectations, a 25% increase in AI adoption is associated with a 1.5% decrease in delivery throughput and a 7.2% decrease in delivery stability. Because AI allows developers to generate code much faster, it often leads to larger batch sizes, which are slower to review and more prone to creating system instability.
evidence.statistic: 25% increase in AI adoption associated with 1.5% drop in throughput and 7.2% drop in stability
evidence.title: Impact of Generative AI in Software Development
evidence.methodology: Global empirical study and developer survey by Google Cloud DORA
evidence.inference: Unchecked AI code output inflates batch sizes and overwhelms code review and CI/CD pipelines, demonstrating workflow and operating model failure.
evidence.framing_bias: DORA frames delivery slowdown as an operating model and team process problem rather than a tool deficiency.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of developer trust in AI-generated outputs and code accuracy
evidence.evidence_quote: Developers who trust generative AI accept more suggestions, submit more change lists, and spend less time searching for information. However, 39% of developers still trust AI outputs “a little” or “not at all,” meaning many teams are missing out on potential productivity gains.
evidence.statistic: 39% of developers trust AI outputs 'a little' or 'not at all'
evidence.title: Impact of Generative AI in Software Development
evidence.methodology: Global empirical study and developer survey by Google Cloud DORA
evidence.inference: Developers lack confidence in AI code correctness and security, leading to low acceptance rates and user trust hurdles.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor frames developer skepticism as a trust/adoption deficit rather than acknowledging code quality or edge case failure rates.

evidence.stated_factor: Clear acceptable-use policies, privacy guidelines, and security guardrails
evidence.evidence_quote: Creating well-defined policies that outline appropriate use cases, data privacy guidelines, and security risks provides developers with a safe framework to operate within. Organizations with clear AI acceptable-use policies show a 451% increase in AI adoption compared to those without.
evidence.statistic: 451% increase in AI adoption in organizations with clear AI acceptable-use policies
evidence.title: Impact of Generative AI in Software Development
evidence.methodology: Global empirical study and developer survey by Google Cloud DORA
evidence.inference: Clear corporate policies on acceptable use, IP boundaries, and data governance eliminate organizational ambiguity, enabling rapid adoption.

evidence.stated_factor: Administrative task time reduction
evidence.evidence_quote: hyperexponential's 2026 Underwriting Edge report, a survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes, backs that skepticism with data: where AI has already reached underwriters, 51% say its biggest contribution so far is time saved on admin, but only 21% say it has improved decision quality.
evidence.statistic: 51% cite time saved on admin as biggest contribution
evidence.title: Intelligent automation in insurance: workflow, data and decisioning
evidence.methodology: survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes and AutoRek 2026 Insurance Report
evidence.inference: Automating mundane administrative overhead provides quantifiable time savings and operational efficiency for underwriters.

evidence.stated_factor: Skepticism over decision quality in underwriting decisioning
evidence.evidence_quote: where AI has already reached underwriters, 51% say its biggest contribution so far is time saved on admin, but only 21% say it has improved decision quality. Part of the skepticism is a product gap, not just a training gap.
evidence.statistic: only 21% say AI has improved decision quality
evidence.title: Intelligent automation in insurance: workflow, data and decisioning
evidence.methodology: survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes and AutoRek 2026 Insurance Report
evidence.inference: Domain experts distrust autonomous decision accuracy on complex risk assessments, requiring proven model reliability before handing over authority.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor contrasts basic admin automation with complex underwriting decisioning to justify purchasing specialized pricing decision engines.

evidence.stated_factor: Legacy system integration, data fragmentation, and AI expertise shortage
evidence.evidence_quote: AutoRek's 2026 Insurance Report found three recurring barriers to scaling AI in carrier operations: legacy system integration challenges, cited by 42% of firms; fragmented data environments, cited by 39%; and a shortage of in-house AI expertise, cited by 40%.
evidence.statistic: 42% cite legacy system integration, 39% fragmented data, 40% lack of in-house AI expertise
evidence.title: Intelligent automation in insurance: workflow, data and decisioning
evidence.methodology: survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes and AutoRek 2026 Insurance Report
evidence.inference: Legacy insurance infrastructure, unstandardized data assets, and lack of specialized in-house AI talent block operational scaling.

evidence.stated_factor: Immature data governance preventing trust in straight-through processing
evidence.evidence_quote: Over half of surveyed firms described their data governance frameworks as early-stage or developing. These gaps compound each other. A carrier with fragmented data cannot fully trust straight-through processing
evidence.statistic: Over 50% describe data governance frameworks as early-stage or developing
evidence.title: Intelligent automation in insurance: workflow, data and decisioning
evidence.methodology: survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes and AutoRek 2026 Insurance Report
evidence.inference: Underwriters cannot trust straight-through automated binding when underlying data sources lack lineage, standardization, and governance.

evidence.stated_factor: Straight-through processing for standard, low-complexity risks
evidence.evidence_quote: One carrier reached quoting and binding in under five minutes with no human involvement for risks under $50,000, according to Datos Insights, by codifying its underwriting rules and decisions in full.
evidence.statistic: quoting and binding in under 5 minutes with no human involvement for risks under $50,000
evidence.title: Intelligent automation in insurance: workflow, data and decisioning
evidence.methodology: survey of 350 CUOs, heads of underwriting, and senior underwriters conducted by Coleman Parkes and AutoRek 2026 Insurance Report
evidence.inference: Codifying underwriting rules into deterministic decision architectures allows straight-through automated policy binding, drastically cutting turnaround time and unit cost.

evidence.stated_factor: Regulatory compliance and legal liability risks under consumer protection statutes for inaccurate automated customer service and dispute handling
use_case_ids: Customer Billing Inquiry & Payment Arrangement Agent
evidence.evidence_quote: We have highlighted that these tools may provide incorrect information, fail to provide meaningful dispute resolution, and raise privacy and security risks. As more companies adopt these types of technology, the CFPB is monitoring compliance with, among other things, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which prohibits discrimination on a prohibited basis in lending transactions, and the Consumer Financial Protection Act, which prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices.
evidence.title: CFPB Comment on Request for Information on Uses, Opportunities, and Risks of Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Services Sector
evidence.methodology: Regulatory comment letter and supervisory market monitoring report
evidence.inference: Federal consumer protection laws enforce strict liability on automated customer servicing, making auditability and regulatory compliance imperative.

evidence.stated_factor: Enforcement scrutiny over automated payment arrangements, debt collection, and financial hardship servicing
use_case_ids: Customer Billing Inquiry & Payment Arrangement Agent
evidence.evidence_quote: These laws apply not only to the origination of credit but also to servicing and debt collection practices, including critical customer service functions like what options companies provide to struggling consumers.
evidence.title: CFPB Comment on Request for Information on Uses, Opportunities, and Risks of Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Services Sector
evidence.methodology: Regulatory comment letter and supervisory market monitoring report
evidence.inference: Regulators target automated debt collection and hardship servicing for compliance violations, preventing autonomous deployment without strict oversight.

evidence.stated_factor: Early maturity stage and narrow initial use cases in proposal workflows
use_case_ids: Enterprise Sales Proposal & Bid Response Generation
RFP Response Generation & Vendor Proposal Evaluation
evidence.evidence_quote: Only 34% of teams have dabbled in the use of generative AI during their RFP process, with the most commonly cited reason for use being help with summarizing information. Although AI usage is not yet very high within the profession, it would seem that fear of the unknown is not the major driving force behind the lack of widespread adoption.
evidence.statistic: Only 34% have used generative AI in RFP process
evidence.title: 10 Things You Need to Know From the 2024 Loopio Trends Report
evidence.methodology: Survey of 1,663 bid and proposal professionals globally conducted in partnership with Loopio
evidence.inference: Immature organizational workflows restrict AI use to basic summarization instead of end-to-end bid management redesign.

evidence.stated_factor: Resistance to autonomous replacement and insistence on human expertise in bids
use_case_ids: Enterprise Sales Proposal & Bid Response Generation
RFP Response Generation & Vendor Proposal Evaluation
evidence.evidence_quote: On the whole, professionals are also confident that AI cannot adequately replace the human element in the RFP process. Between 75% and 82% of bid and proposal professionals from associate to VP level stated that they would not consider replacing people resources with AI; although this figure was only 52% among C-level executives.
evidence.statistic: 75% to 82% would not consider replacing people resources with AI
evidence.title: 10 Things You Need to Know From the 2024 Loopio Trends Report
evidence.methodology: Survey of 1,663 bid and proposal professionals globally conducted in partnership with Loopio
evidence.inference: Proposal professionals resist autonomous automation due to fear of job displacement and conviction that nuanced domain expertise cannot be automated.
evidence.framing_bias: Industry association protects human practitioner relevance by stressing that bids require bespoke human relationship and expertise.

evidence.stated_factor: Rising RFP volume and team burnout driving demand for proposal automation
use_case_ids: Enterprise Sales Proposal & Bid Response Generation
RFP Response Generation & Vendor Proposal Evaluation
evidence.evidence_quote: Teams are responding to more RFPs this year – an average of 175, up from 162 last year – and 44% of teams reported that they responded to more RFPs in 2023 than previous years... Teams who report unmanageable stress levels report that they are spending around 14 more hours on writing their RFP responses, but have a win rate that is 7% lower.
evidence.statistic: Average 175 RFPs responded to; 44% reporting higher volume

evidence.stated_factor: Consumer trust and autonomy boundaries (privacy, override controls, human backup)

evidence.title: Retailers say agentic AI is the best way to boost customer sales
evidence.methodology: Survey of 8,350 shoppers and 1,700 retail industry decision-makers across 25 countries
evidence.inference: Customer willingness to interact with autonomous agents requires explicit human override controls, auditability of financial transactions, and strict data privacy.
evidence.framing_bias: Source treats critical governance, auditability, and kill-switch capabilities as consumer trust preferences.

evidence.stated_factor: Early technological and architectural maturity for complex multi-agent execution in banking
evidence.evidence_quote: It is early days for generative AI (GenAI) adoption at banks. And even earlier days for agentic AI adoption. Celent anticipates the current wave of GenAI adoption by banks will remain focused on advancing intelligent virtual assistants (IVAs) that respond to queries and requests from employees and customers.
evidence.title: Shedding Light on Agentic AI in Banking
evidence.methodology: Analyst research report analyzing AI adoption trends across global banks
evidence.inference: Banks face architectural and process immaturity, limiting near-term adoption to basic assistive copilots rather than autonomous multi-agent systems.

evidence.stated_factor: Agent chaining potential across end-to-end multi-step banking workflows and customer journeys
evidence.evidence_quote: Celent believes that agent chaining (combining specialized agents to support a workflow or customer journey) will have profound impact in numerous areas of banking across lines of business.
evidence.title: Shedding Light on Agentic AI in Banking
evidence.methodology: Analyst research report analyzing AI adoption trends across global banks
evidence.inference: Agent chaining offers the architectural ability to orchestrate complex multi-step banking workflows, driving significant end-to-end operational efficiency.
evidence.framing_bias: Analyst projects transformative potential for agent chaining while actual production deployments remain nascent.

evidence.stated_factor: Automating operational onboarding, documentation, and compliance workloads
evidence.evidence_quote: Over two-in-three (70%) bank employees are focused on operational activities, rising to 91% for those employees on customer onboarding teams, leaving little time for customer interactions... The report determines that banks could optimize up to 66% of the time spent on operations, documentation, compliance, and other onboarding-related activities through AI-powered intelligent transformation and generative AI copilots.
evidence.statistic: Banks could optimize up to 66% of operational time in onboarding and compliance; onboarding teams spend 91% of time on ops/compliance
evidence.title: World Retail Banking Report 2024: Only 6% of retail banks have built an enterprise roadmap to drive AI-driven transformation at scale
evidence.methodology: Global survey of 250 retail banking executives, 1,500 banking employees, and 4,500 banking customers across 14 markets
evidence.inference: Automating repetitive onboarding, documentation, and compliance tasks frees high-cost banking staff from operational drag to focus on revenue-generating interactions.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy models aggressive theoretical time-saving estimates (up to 66%) to build demand for AI advisory services.

evidence.stated_factor: Upgrading legacy deflection bots to conversational AI and agent assist copilots to resolve customer dissatisfaction
evidence.evidence_quote: Nearly two-in-three (61%) bank customers contacted agents because they were unhappy with chatbot resolutions, while 17% simply distrusted chatbots and preferred human agents... According to the report, banks should create intelligent contact centers that leverage chatbots with conversational AI capabilities and intelligent copilots to assist agents in their day-to-day tasks.
evidence.statistic: 61% of bank customers contacted human agents due to dissatisfaction with rule-based chatbots
evidence.title: World Retail Banking Report 2024: Only 6% of retail banks have built an enterprise roadmap to drive AI-driven transformation at scale
evidence.methodology: Global survey of 250 retail banking executives, 1,500 banking employees, and 4,500 banking customers across 14 markets
evidence.inference: Poor accuracy and rigid rule-based chatbot failures force banks to upgrade to modern generative conversational AI and agent-assist copilots to restore customer trust.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy reframes historical chatbot failures as a reason to buy next-generation generative AI solutions.

evidence.stated_factor: Enterprise readiness deficits and absence of AI impact tracking KPIs
evidence.evidence_quote: Globally, only 4% of retail banks achieved a high score on business commitment and technology capabilities, while 41% scored average, indicating a widespread lack of readiness to embrace and effectively implement intelligent transformation... among those surveyed, just 6% of banks have established key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure AI impact and continuous monitoring.
evidence.statistic: Only 4% of retail banks demonstrate high readiness; only 6% have roadmaps or KPIs established
evidence.title: World Retail Banking Report 2024: Only 6% of retail banks have built an enterprise roadmap to drive AI-driven transformation at scale
evidence.methodology: Global survey of 250 retail banking executives, 1,500 banking employees, and 4,500 banking customers across 14 markets
evidence.inference: Widespread lack of strategic leadership commitment, architectural readiness, and formal ROI measurement metrics blocks banks from scaling AI initiatives.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy emphasizes enterprise immaturity (only 4% high readiness) to sell organizational readiness and KPI advisory frameworks.

evidence.stated_factor: Transition toward higher-level autonomous networks and zero-touch operations
evidence.evidence_quote: Eighty-eight percent of organizations report being between levels 1-3 of autonomy, as defined by the TM Forum, and the use of generative AI and agentic AI is expected to accelerate the shift to level 5 autonomous networks.
evidence.statistic: 88% of organizations currently at TM Forum autonomy levels 1-3
evidence.title: Survey Reveals AI Advances in Telecom: Networks and Automation in Driver's Seat as Return on Investment Climbs
evidence.methodology: fourth annual global survey of 1,000 telecommunications professionals and operators
evidence.inference: Telcos are re-architecting operational workflows and platform strategies to transition toward autonomous, zero-touch network operations.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor frames autonomy levels using TM Forum standards to present infrastructure upgrades as an architectural inevitability.

evidence.stated_factor: Cross-domain autonomous decision-making without human delay
evidence.evidence_quote: Generative AI delivered fast productivity gains, but agentic AI is where telecoms begin to see structural ROI... Autonomous agents can act across networks, IT and customer journeys, turning insights into decisions without human delay.
evidence.title: Survey Reveals AI Advances in Telecom: Networks and Automation in Driver's Seat as Return on Investment Climbs
evidence.methodology: fourth annual global survey of 1,000 telecommunications professionals and operators
evidence.inference: Cross-domain autonomous decision-making removes human processing bottlenecks and latency, unlocking structural operational efficiencies across IT, networks, and customer journeys.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor contrasts GenAI productivity with agentic AI 'structural ROI' to sell comprehensive autonomous platform stacks.

evidence.stated_factor: Customer preference for human-in-the-loop support during high-stakes or complex service interactions
evidence.evidence_quote: Technology reduces stress for 65% of shoppers, but human support is essential for complex purchases. Preference for in-person assistance has surged: 74% value it during in-store service, and 66% during purchase decisions.
evidence.statistic: 74% value human support during in-store service; 66% during purchase decisions
evidence.title: What matters to today's consumer 2026
evidence.methodology: Survey of 12,000 consumers across 12 countries
evidence.inference: Consumers lack trust in automated agents for high-stakes or complex transactions, preferring human interaction and established retail habits.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy frames retail consumer behavior to advise hybrid human-AI customer service designs.

evidence.stated_factor: Consumer adoption and demand for conversational AI shopping and assistance tools
evidence.evidence_quote: One-quarter (25%) of consumers have already used Gen AI shopping tools in 2025, while a further 31% plan to use them in the future... Technology reduces stress for 65% of shoppers
evidence.statistic: 25% have used Gen AI shopping tools; 31% plan to use them; 65% say technology reduces stress
evidence.title: What matters to today's consumer 2026
evidence.methodology: Survey of 12,000 consumers across 12 countries
evidence.inference: Adoption is driven by rapidly shifting consumer habits and growing trust/comfort with conversational AI assistants for shopping support.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy presents consumer willingness to use tools as an urgent driver for retailers to invest in conversational commerce.

evidence.stated_factor: addressing administrative burden through automation
evidence.evidence_quote: The top area of opportunity for AI according to 57% of physicians surveyed in 2024 was 'addressing administrative burden through automation,' up slightly from 56% in 2023.
evidence.statistic: 57% of physicians
evidence.title: AMA: Physician enthusiasm grows for health care AI
evidence.methodology: Survey of US physicians tracking sentiment shifts from August 2023 to November 2024
evidence.inference: Physician adoption is primarily motivated by reducing administrative documentation burdens and EHR charting overhead to reclaim clinical productivity.

evidence.stated_factor: patient data privacy assurances
evidence.evidence_quote: According to physicians surveyed in 2024, the top attributes required to advance physician adoption of AI tools were a designated feedback channel (88%), data privacy assurances (87%), and EHR integration (84%).
evidence.statistic: 87% require data privacy assurances
evidence.title: AMA: Physician enthusiasm grows for health care AI
evidence.methodology: Survey of US physicians tracking sentiment shifts from August 2023 to November 2024
evidence.inference: Physicians require strict assurances around patient privacy and PHI data governance to prevent unauthorized data sharing or breach of healthcare privacy laws.

evidence.stated_factor: concerns over medical liability for model errors
evidence.evidence_quote: In 2023, the top attributes were data privacy assurances (87%), not being held liable for AI model errors (87%), and medical liability coverage (86%).
evidence.statistic: 87% require not being held liable for AI errors
evidence.title: AMA: Physician enthusiasm grows for health care AI
evidence.methodology: Survey of US physicians tracking sentiment shifts from August 2023 to November 2024
evidence.inference: Adoption is stalled by unclear medico-legal liability and malpractice exposure if an AI system generates inaccurate clinical outputs or hallucinations.

evidence.stated_factor: Rapid rise of consumer AI assistants across pre-purchase product research and deal discovery
evidence.evidence_quote: From assistants to agents, AI is reshaping the shopping journey. Nearly three-quarters (72%) of consumers still shop in stores, but AI-assisted shopping is emerging: 41% use AI assistants to research products, 33% to look for reviews, and 31% to search for deals. Brands and retailers must orchestrate the converged experience no matter where the journey begins or ends.
evidence.statistic: 41% use AI assistants to research products, 33% for reviews, 31% to search for deals
evidence.title: Own the agentic commerce experience
evidence.publisher: National Retail Federation and IBM Institute for Business Value
evidence.methodology: Survey of 18,000 global consumers and survey of retail and consumer products leaders across 26 countries
evidence.inference: Surging consumer adoption of AI assistants across pre-purchase research is forcing brands to redesign their customer engagement and commerce operating models.
evidence.framing_bias: Industry body and consultancy co-report highlights shifting shopper behavior to push retailers toward digital commerce transformation.

evidence.stated_factor: High-volume transaction surveillance, fraud detection, and customer support automation
evidence.evidence_quote: Regarding use cases, AI is most frequently employed in areas such as client and transaction profiling (for commercial purposes) and customer support... Additionally, AI plays a role in fraud and AML/CFT efforts, where it is used to analyse vast amounts of data and detect patterns indicative of illicit activities.
evidence.title: Risk Assessment Report: Special topic – Artificial intelligence
evidence.methodology: EBA Risk Assessment Questionnaire (RAQ) surveying EU/EEA banks and stakeholder workshop findings
evidence.inference: Banks leverage AI to process massive transaction volumes for AML/fraud surveillance and customer service at lower marginal costs than manual review.

evidence.stated_factor: Operational efficiency and customer interaction gains driving production rollouts
evidence.evidence_quote: Approximately one-third of respondent EU banks have already implemented GPAI in at least one-use case (Figure 75) highlighting the sector's growing recognition of its potential to drive efficiencies, enhance customer interactions, and generate new business insights.
evidence.statistic: Approximately one-third of respondent EU banks have already implemented GPAI in at least one use case
evidence.title: Risk Assessment Report: Special topic – Artificial intelligence
evidence.methodology: EBA Risk Assessment Questionnaire (RAQ) surveying EU/EEA banks and stakeholder workshop findings
evidence.inference: Financial institutions deploy GPAI into production driven by tangible operational efficiencies, reduced handling costs, and improved customer interaction speeds.

evidence.stated_factor: High concentration of realized value in customer service, network operations, and sales
evidence.evidence_quote: In the survey, approximately 72% of realized value is concentrated in three domains: customer service, network operations, and marketing & sales, areas where cost, service quality, and growth decisions are tightly linked.
evidence.statistic: Approximately 72% of realized value concentrated in three domains
evidence.title: Closing the Generative AI Readiness Gap: What Telco Leaders Do Differently
evidence.methodology: 2025 Telco Generative AI Readiness Survey of 109 senior telecom executives worldwide
evidence.inference: AI value concentrates in high-volume core workflows (customer service, network ops, sales) where operational cost savings directly feed the bottom line.

evidence.stated_factor: Autonomy as an economic necessity to eliminate human-in-the-loop latency and cost at scale
evidence.evidence_quote: once scale is reached in high-volume, labor-intensive areas, autonomy becomes an economic necessity. Beyond certain volumes of tickets, faults, or campaigns, keeping humans in every loop adds cost and delay that erodes much of the value generative AI can create.
evidence.title: Closing the Generative AI Readiness Gap: What Telco Leaders Do Differently
evidence.methodology: 2025 Telco Generative AI Readiness Survey of 109 senior telecom executives worldwide
evidence.inference: Human-in-the-loop latency and staffing costs at high volume become financially unsustainable, compelling organizations to transition to autonomous agentic architectures.

evidence.stated_factor: Pilot congestion and proof-of-concept stagnation
evidence.evidence_quote: They have bold targets and a large number of initiatives, but lack the alignment, governance, and embedded capabilities to deliver at scale. The pattern is familiar: dozens of projects, more than half stalling at the proof-of-concept stage, and a limited trace of impact on the P&L. The result is pilot congestion and ROI leakage.
evidence.statistic: More than half of projects stalling at proof-of-concept stage
evidence.title: Closing the Generative AI Readiness Gap: What Telco Leaders Do Differently
evidence.methodology: 2025 Telco Generative AI Readiness Survey of 109 senior telecom executives worldwide
evidence.inference: Pilot congestion and PoC stagnation result from a lack of enterprise operating model alignment, executive ownership, and clear paths to P&L realization.
evidence.framing_bias: Strategy consultancy diagnoses pilot congestion to sell enterprise operating model redesign and strategic governance services.

evidence.stated_factor: Governance deficits and undefined enterprise autonomy thresholds
evidence.evidence_quote: only about one in four operators reports full alignment between AI and commercial strategy... autonomy also shifts accountability away from individual users and toward the enterprise. That increases pressure to define decision rights, escalation paths, and financial controls. For many telcos, governance readiness, more than technology, is becoming the constraint.
evidence.statistic: Only about one in four operators (25%) reports full alignment between AI and commercial strategy
evidence.title: Closing the Generative AI Readiness Gap: What Telco Leaders Do Differently
evidence.methodology: 2025 Telco Generative AI Readiness Survey of 109 senior telecom executives worldwide
evidence.inference: Deploying autonomous systems requires shifting accountability from users to enterprise risk frameworks, exposing deficits in decision rights and auditability.

evidence.stated_factor: Talent shortages, integration complexity, and model performance risks
evidence.evidence_quote: Operators cite challenges such as talent shortages, integration complexity, and data/security/model-performance issues. The implication is straightforward: breadth becomes expensive quickly.
evidence.title: Closing the Generative AI Readiness Gap: What Telco Leaders Do Differently
evidence.methodology: 2025 Telco Generative AI Readiness Survey of 109 senior telecom executives worldwide
evidence.inference: Broad AI rollouts are inhibited by technical talent shortages, complex legacy integrations, and unpredictable model quality/security.

evidence.stated_factor: Efficiency, speed, and accuracy improvements across claims and underwriting
evidence.evidence_quote: Across the value chain, AI is already increasing efficiency and accuracy in areas like operations, claims, and underwriting, and we expect its impact to continue growing as insurers innovate further in the years to come... operations and claims processing represent key areas where insurers are integrating AI to improve efficiency and decision-making.
evidence.statistic: 55% in early or full adoption; 90% in some stage of evaluation
evidence.title: Conning Releases 2025 Survey on AI & Insurance Technology: The C-Suite Verdict
evidence.methodology: Survey of top US insurance C-suite executives across Life/Annuity (44%), P&C (44%), and multiline insurers
evidence.inference: Insurers adopt AI to drive down claims turnaround times and operational processing costs while improving decision accuracy in underwriting.

evidence.stated_factor: Expanded attack surface and cyber risk entry points introduced by advanced AI integrations
evidence.evidence_quote: Cyber risk both created and mitigated by AI – While advanced tech increases potential entry points for cyber-attacks, AI also revolutionizes insurers’ threat detection and mitigation strategies.
evidence.title: Conning Releases 2025 Survey on AI & Insurance Technology: The C-Suite Verdict
evidence.methodology: Survey of top US insurance C-suite executives across Life/Annuity (44%), P&C (44%), and multiline insurers
evidence.inference: Enterprise AI adoption expands the attack surface by introducing new software vulnerabilities, credential exposure points, and external cyber attack vectors.

evidence.stated_factor: Workforce skills gap and need for literacy and workflow realignment
evidence.evidence_quote: As AI streamlines repetitive tasks, industry roles will be adjusted to value more customer relationship skills and technological literacy, demanding new skills and thus reshaping the traditional career ladder.
evidence.title: Conning Releases 2025 Survey on AI & Insurance Technology: The C-Suite Verdict
evidence.methodology: Survey of top US insurance C-suite executives across Life/Annuity (44%), P&C (44%), and multiline insurers
evidence.inference: Shifting repetitive tasks to AI creates internal workforce skill gaps and necessitates role redesign, change management, and technical upskilling.

evidence.stated_factor: Cost savings across compliance, risk management, and client engagement operations
evidence.evidence_quote: The results showed that 95% of firms have scaled their adoption to multiple use cases, with an overwhelming 78% already exploring agentic AI to unlock deeper strategic advantages. Much of the GenAI activity is focused on use cases that support proactive client engagement and real-time risk management... Many initial deployments of GenAI have delivered clear operational successes across compliance, risk management and IT infrastructure for both wealth managers and asset managers.
evidence.statistic: 78% of wealth and asset managers are exploring agentic AI; 95% scaled to multiple use cases
evidence.title: Unlocking strategic advantage: Generative AI in wealth and asset management
evidence.methodology: Survey of 100 wealth and asset management executives managing up to $25T in AUM
evidence.inference: Wealth and asset managers scale GenAI and explore agents because initial implementations demonstrated clear cost reductions and operational efficiencies.

evidence.stated_factor: Regulatory complexities, hallucinations, model bias, and trust deficits in client advisory outputs
evidence.evidence_quote: While regulatory and privacy issues are top concerns, inaccuracies, hallucinations and model bias continue to be areas that need work. Some of these core issues around back-end data can prevent users from fully trusting outputs and ultimately impact adoption. Regulatory and compliance complexities surprised 86% of firms.
evidence.statistic: Regulatory and compliance complexities surprised 86% of firms
evidence.title: Unlocking strategic advantage: Generative AI in wealth and asset management
evidence.methodology: Survey of 100 wealth and asset management executives managing up to $25T in AUM
evidence.inference: Adoption in wealth management is held back by strict regulatory rules, unpredictable model hallucinations and bias, and user trust deficits in advisory outputs.

evidence.stated_factor: High operational AI usage and expanding technology investment across retail functions
evidence.evidence_quote: The survey of 1,000 retail professionals across marketing, IT, data and executive leadership reveals that 45% of retailers are already using AI daily or several times per week, and 97% plan to maintain or increase their AI investment in the coming year. However, only 11% say they’re fully prepared to deploy AI tools at scale.
evidence.statistic: 45% use AI daily or weekly; 97% maintain/increase investment; only 11% prepared to scale
evidence.title: Retailers Are All-In on AI - But Disconnected Data Threatens Progress
evidence.methodology: Survey of 1,000 retail professionals across marketing, IT, data and executive leadership
evidence.inference: High daily usage among staff and sustained executive budget allocation drive continued enterprise commitment to AI initiatives.
evidence.framing_bias: Data vendor highlights high usage and enterprise optimism to create urgency before highlighting readiness gaps.

evidence.stated_factor: Fragmented customer data, tool costs, and technical expertise shortages
evidence.evidence_quote: Despite high levels of optimism, the report reveals several key barriers: 58% of respondents say their customer data is fragmented or incomplete, 46% cite high costs of AI tools as a top challenge, 35% note limited technical expertise, and only 21% are “very confident” in their ability to understand and act on customer data.
evidence.statistic: 58% report fragmented/incomplete customer data; 46% cite high tool costs; 35% cite limited expertise
evidence.title: Retailers Are All-In on AI - But Disconnected Data Threatens Progress
evidence.methodology: Survey of 1,000 retail professionals across marketing, IT, data and executive leadership
evidence.inference: Inability to ground retail AI agents on clean customer data due to fragmented silos, high software tool costs, and technical skill gaps hinders scaling.
evidence.framing_bias: Customer Data Platform vendor emphasizes customer data fragmentation as the primary hurdle to sell its data unification platform.

evidence.stated_factor: Existential margin compression and operating cost pressures
evidence.evidence_quote: Telecom operators face a familiar squeeze: data traffic keeps rising, networks require continued investment, and traditional connectivity revenues are growing too slowly to absorb the pressure. AI can help telecoms run leaner, which itself is valuable. But the bigger opportunity is to use AI to help telecoms grow differently. That approach will address what many telecom CEOs see as an existential concern: 55% of industry CEOs in PwC’s 2025 CEO survey said that their company will not be economically viable in a decade if it stays on its current path.
evidence.statistic: 55% of telecom CEOs say company will not be viable in a decade on current path
evidence.title: Telecom companies have an AI advantage. Can they convert it into growth?
evidence.methodology: PwC AI performance study surveying 1,217 senior executives across 25 sectors globally, alongside PwC Global CEO Survey
evidence.inference: Severe margin compression, stagnant revenue growth, and escalating infrastructure capex force telecom operators to adopt AI agents to drastically lower operational costs and preserve economic viability.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy frames the economic squeeze as an existential viability threat to accelerate large-scale AI transformation programs.

evidence.stated_factor: Lagging enterprise-wide scaling capabilities and operating model inertia
evidence.evidence_quote: Telecoms are better prepared to use AI than the average company, but most aren’t yet engaging in the practices that scale the technology across the enterprise and change the operating model... they trail the companies seeing the highest returns from AI (the ‘AI leaders’) in the capabilities that enable the technology to scale.
evidence.title: Telecom companies have an AI advantage. Can they convert it into growth?
evidence.methodology: PwC AI performance study surveying 1,217 senior executives across 25 sectors globally, alongside PwC Global CEO Survey
evidence.inference: Telecom AI adoption is bottlenecked by organizational inertia, lack of executive leadership, and failure to redesign legacy operating models required to scale beyond isolated pilots.
evidence.framing_bias: Consultancy contrasts average telecoms with 'AI leaders' to create competitive urgency and pitch operating model advisory services.

evidence.stated_factor: Rapid production deployment of autonomous specialized AI agents
evidence.evidence_quote: 56% of telco executives reported their organizations are actively using AI agents in production, with nearly half (43%) saying they have already launched ten or more. Notably, one in five respondents also said these agents are deeply embedded across their operations.
evidence.statistic: 56% actively using AI agents in production; 43% launched 10 or more
evidence.title: How AI agents are reshaping the telecommunications industry
evidence.methodology: survey of 489 senior telecommunications leaders conducted by National Research Group for Google Cloud
evidence.inference: Telecoms are embedding specialized autonomous agents directly into production workflows, reflecting active operating model modernization.
evidence.framing_bias: Cloud vendor highlights high production penetration metrics (56% in production, 43% with 10+ agents) to generate FOMO and accelerate cloud infrastructure adoption.

evidence.stated_factor: Deployment across security, customer service, network remediation, and field operations
evidence.evidence_quote: applications with broader organizational focus are the leading areas for deploying AI agents, with security (47%), technical support (46%), and customer service and experience (45%) coming in as the top use cases. However, the survey also indicated that the biggest opportunities for AI agents are industry-specific use cases... network remediation (34%), network agents (32%) and field operations assistants (31%)
evidence.statistic: 47% security, 46% tech support, 45% customer service, 34% network remediation, 31% field assist
evidence.title: How AI agents are reshaping the telecommunications industry
evidence.methodology: survey of 489 senior telecommunications leaders conducted by National Research Group for Google Cloud
evidence.inference: Telecom operators are adopting AI agents across both horizontal support functions and vertical domain-specific operations (network remediation, field operations) to automate core business processes.
evidence.framing_bias: Cloud hyperscaler showcases widespread multi-departmental deployment to promote its platform as an all-in-one foundation for both IT and telecom network operations.

evidence.stated_factor: Data privacy, security, system integration, and scalability constraints
evidence.evidence_quote: Around one in three executives (35%) indicated that data privacy and security is a top consideration when choosing an LLM provider, followed by scalability and performance (27%), integration with existing systems (26%), and cost (25%).
evidence.statistic: 35% cite data privacy/security, 27% scalability/performance, 26% legacy integration, 25% cost
evidence.title: How AI agents are reshaping the telecommunications industry
evidence.methodology: survey of 489 senior telecommunications leaders conducted by National Research Group for Google Cloud
evidence.inference: Agent adoption in telecoms is constrained by foundational enterprise prerequisites: strict data privacy boundaries, agent security/identity, legacy OSS/BSS integration hurdles, and infrastructure cost/scalability.
evidence.framing_bias: Cloud provider packages major enterprise adoption barriers into vendor-evaluation criteria to highlight its enterprise security, integration, and compliance credentials.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of internal AI/ML expertise and low organizational capabilities
evidence.evidence_quote: According to Incisiv, only 19% of retailers rate their AI/ML capabilities as "industry leading" or "above average," and 46% still struggle to link physical and digital touchpoints... Meanwhile, Incisiv research shows that 50% of organizations report that their limited internal AI/ML expertise is a barrier to modernization.
evidence.statistic: only 19% rate capabilities above average; 50% cite limited internal AI/ML expertise as a barrier
evidence.title: The Role of AI Shopping Assistants in 2026
evidence.methodology: Incisiv retail and grocery digital benchmark study and analysis
evidence.inference: Retailers face severe talent shortages and organizational skill gaps in AI/ML engineering, hindering their ability to build, maintain, and modernize agentic shopping workflows.
evidence.framing_bias: Industry analyst highlights internal expertise deficits to advocate for pre-packaged third-party SaaS solutions and advisory support.

evidence.stated_factor: Backend system integration barriers across inventory, order orchestration, and catalog data
evidence.evidence_quote: The best AI assistants do not just answer questions. They act. They check real-time inventory across channels... This requires deep integration and having the right data in place and organized correctly to enable action. Product catalogs. Inventory systems. Customer profiles. Order orchestration. Logistics networks. When these connect, assistants become valuable. When they do not, they guess.
evidence.statistic: 46% struggle to link physical and digital touchpoints
evidence.title: The Role of AI Shopping Assistants in 2026
evidence.methodology: Incisiv retail and grocery digital benchmark study and analysis
evidence.inference: Actionable shopping agents require deep real-time connectivity into fragmented legacy backends (inventory, ERP, OMS, logistics); without reliable connectors and harmonized catalog data, agents cannot execute transactions.
evidence.framing_bias: Analyst draws a sharp contrast between static chatbots and action-oriented assistants to drive investment into omnichannel systems integration.

evidence.stated_factor: Consumer preference for human assistance for nuanced service, returns, and complaints
evidence.evidence_quote: Privacy concerns also linger, and most shoppers prefer speaking to a person for nuanced requests, returns, or complaints.
evidence.title: The Role of AI Shopping Assistants in 2026
evidence.methodology: Incisiv retail and grocery digital benchmark study and analysis
evidence.inference: Customer distrust, privacy concerns, and model accuracy/empathy limitations in handling nuanced or contentious issues (returns, disputes) inhibit fully autonomous customer service adoption.

evidence.stated_factor: Cross-departmental automated decision-making and dynamic forecasting
evidence.evidence_quote: Agentic AI is reshaping business operations by enabling automated decision-making, dynamic forecasting, and adaptive customer interactions across multiple departments, from sales and marketing to operations and cybersecurity.
evidence.title: AI Demands More: Enterprises Are Playing Catch-Up on Mission-Critical Data Modernization
evidence.methodology: survey and interviews of 151 CSP leaders across North America, EMEA, and Asia conducted by IDC
evidence.inference: Organizations adopt agentic AI to enable autonomous cross-functional orchestration, unifying decision-making and forecasting across traditionally siloed operational departments.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor-sponsored research emphasizes seamless multi-departmental automation to position broad enterprise software suites.

evidence.stated_factor: Internal enterprise data inaccessibility and poor data health
evidence.evidence_quote: The emergence of powerful agentic AI technologies to orchestrate workflows and autonomous decision-making across multiple AI models will require most organizations to invest in data modernization to ensure the levels of end-to-end data health, security and accessibility needed to deliver reliable AI results... The typical service provider estimates that just 50% of internal data is currently accessible by the organization's AI models and analytics.
evidence.statistic: Only 50% of internal telecom data is accessible to AI models and analytics
evidence.title: AI Demands More: Enterprises Are Playing Catch-Up on Mission-Critical Data Modernization
evidence.methodology: survey and interviews of 151 CSP leaders across North America, EMEA, and Asia conducted by IDC
evidence.inference: Autonomous agent execution is blocked because half of enterprise telecom data is trapped in inaccessible legacy silos, lacking data governance, standard schemas, and pipeline health.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor Amdocs highlights data inaccessibility to create urgency for its data modernization and integration software offerings.

evidence.stated_factor: Lack of integrated AI governance policies and platforms
evidence.evidence_quote: Only 19% of communications service providers worldwide have fully implemented an integrated set of processes, platforms and governance policies required to support effective data modernization for AI.
evidence.statistic: Only 19% of CSPs have fully implemented integrated AI data governance
evidence.title: AI Demands More: Enterprises Are Playing Catch-Up on Mission-Critical Data Modernization
evidence.methodology: survey and interviews of 151 CSP leaders across North America, EMEA, and Asia conducted by IDC
evidence.inference: Agent adoption is impeded by the absence of enterprise data governance frameworks, classification standards, and operational policies needed to securely ground AI agents on enterprise assets.
evidence.framing_bias: Vendor frames the low governance maturity (19%) as a platform deficit to sell unified governance and data platforms.

evidence.stated_factor: Automated SecOps threat detection and compliance auditing via AI agents
evidence.evidence_quote: According to the State of IT research, over 40% of IT security teams already use agents in their day-to-day operations — a figure that’s anticipated to nearly double over the next two years... Three quarters (75%) expect to use AI agents within two years — up from 41% today.
evidence.statistic: 41% currently use agents; 75% expect to use within two years
evidence.title: Salesforce Research: IT Security Stats for 2025
evidence.methodology: double-anonymous survey of over 2,000 enterprise IT security, privacy, and compliance decision-makers across 28 countries
evidence.inference: Severe cybersecurity talent shortages and threat volume drive adoption of autonomous agents to automate SecOps incident triage, patch management, and continuous compliance auditing.
evidence.framing_bias: Salesforce frames SecOps agent adoption as surging rapidly to validate its enterprise agent platform (Agentforce) across security workflows.

evidence.stated_factor: Data foundation deficiencies and lacking agentic guardrails
evidence.evidence_quote: Nearly half (48%) worry their data foundation isn’t set up to get the most out of agentic AI, and over half (55%) aren’t fully confident they have the appropriate guardrails to deploy AI agents.
